KEY TAKEAWAYS: • Emotional regulation difficulties can accompany ADHD, including irritability and low frustration tolerance. • Anger may sometimes come with embarrassment, hurt, or overwhelm. Show this video to your child with ADHD, aged 7 and up. 💛 How the wrong friends can affect your child with ADHD — even when they have a good heart. 💛 Kids with ADHD often have the biggest hearts in the room. They're loyal, funny, generous, and they want to be liked so badly. But that big heart, mixed with impulsivity, can make them more vulnerable to peer pressure. "Dare you to throw it." "Say it to the teacher — it'll be funny." "If you're really my friend, you'll do it." Some children with ADHD may act before thinking through the consequences. And a child who's felt left out before may say yes just to belong. Then they're the one who gets caught. The one who gets blamed. The one who gets the reputation — while the "friend" walks away. Here's what we talk about at home: 💛 What a real friend does: — Likes you even when you say no — Doesn't laugh at you to look cool — Never asks you to do something that could hurt you or someone else — Sticks around when you're in trouble 🚩 Signs someone might not be a good friend: — They only seem to like you when you take risks — They dare you, then stand back and watch — They tell you to keep secrets from trusted grown-ups — You often feel worried or bad after spending time with them 🛑 How to say no (practise it together!): "Nah, I'm good." "My mum wouldn't want me to do that." "I don't want to." Then walk away and find a trusted grown-up or another friend. For parents: ✅ Role-play tricky moments at home, so the words come more easily when your child needs them. ✅ Encourage healthy friendships — even one supportive friend can make a difference. ✅ Ask gently, "How did you feel after playing with them?" ✅ Never shame your child for wanting to be liked. Help them find people who appreciate them for who they are. Your child doesn't need to change their heart. They deserve friends who respect it. 💛 Watch this together, then ask: "Who makes you feel good about yourself?" 👇 📚 Want to help your child with ADHD navigate friendships and everyday challenges? Fermentowana kapusta🫰zainwestuj w zdrowe jelita i naturalnie wspieraj swoją odporność☺️ Kapusta fermentowana z burakami, marchewką i czosnkiem🫠 Składniki: * 1 Kapusta pokrojona w paseczki * 1 duża marchewka, pokrojona w cienkie plasterki * 2 buraki, pokrojone w cienkie plasterki * 3-4 ząbki czosnku * 1 pęczek natki pietruszki * Liście laurowe * Garść ziaren pieprzu czarnego lub kolorowego * 1 łyżka soli na 1 litr wody Przygotowanie: 1. Kapustę pokrój w paseczki, a marchewkę i buraki w cienkie plasterki. 2. Do czystego słoika wkładaj warstwami kapustę, marchewkę, buraki, czosnek i natkę pietruszki. 3. Dodaj liście laurowe oraz ziarna pieprzu. 4. Przygotuj solankę, rozpuszczając 1 łyżkę soli w 1 litrze wody. 5. Zalej warzywa solanką tak, aby były całkowicie przykryte. Dociśnij je, żeby nie wypływały ponad powierzchnię. 6. Pozostaw słoik w temperaturze pokojowej na około 8 dni. Warzywa muszą być cały czas zanurzone w solance. 7. Po 8 dniach wstaw słoik do lodówki, aby spowolnić fermentację. Kiedy można jeść? Kiszonka może być gotowa do spożycia już po 12-14 dniach, jeśli prawidłowo fermentowała. Powinna mieć przyjemny, kwaśny zapach i smak. Czas fermentacji zależy od temperatury oraz przebiegu kiszenia. Ważne: Warzywa muszą być cały czas przykryte solanką. Jeśli pojawi się pleśń lub nieprzyjemny, gnilny zapach, nie spożywaj kiszonki. If you’ve ever seen videos of Polish high school students dressed elegantly and dancing the Polonez, there’s a beautiful tradition behind it. Studniówka is Poland’s traditional school ball held roughly 100 days before the Matura, the final secondary-school examinations. And traditionally, the evening begins with the Polonez. 🇵🇱 This stately Polish dance has centuries of history and became an important symbol of Polish culture and national identity. For students, dancing it at Studniówka marks a real milestone — the beginning of the final countdown to finishing school and stepping into adult life. Teachers, parents and students spend weeks preparing, and when those first notes begin, generations of Polish students are connected by the same tradition. It’s more than just a school dance. POV: You’ve just landed in Krakow and no one told you this 🇵🇱‼️ We saw SO many tourists get scammed, ripped off or suffer for doing these. 1. Public drinking: Drinking alcohol in parks, streets, or open public spaces is illegal and carries immediate fines.  2. Traffic rules: Police strictly enforce jaywalking and red-light violations for pedestrians, and traffic fines apply equally to visitors. 3. Public transport: Always buy and validate your ticket immediately upon boarding, as plainclothes inspectors check fares frequently.  4. Politics and religion: Avoid bringing up sensitive political debates or joking about Catholicism, which remains deeply rooted in traditional culture. 5. Street promoters: Ignore people handing out flyers or inviting you into clubs and basement bars in old towns (especially in Kraków), as overcharging and scams are well-documented. 6. Eating in main square: prices are inflated and the food isn’t always the best.  7. Sunday shopping: Do not plan major grocery or retail shopping on Sundays, as most large supermarkets and stores are legally closed. 8. Euronet ATMs: Avoid standalone Euronet ATMs, which charge high foreign conversion fees and markup rates; use bank-affiliated ATMs (such as PKO BP, Santander, or Millenium) instead. 9. Currency exchange offices: they are overpriced and offer bad exchange rates.  10. High roaming charges: most providers charge high roaming costs in Poland. Consider buying an e-sim before your trip. We used Saily. Code: CAEXPLORE for money off. Our biggest mistakes? 2 and 9 - learn from us! SAVE this for your trip & send it to who you’re going to Krakow with.
